subject: POC: Trial agenda, model selection & acceptance criteria (RetailX)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: POC: Trial agenda, model selection & acceptance criteria (RetailX)

Hi Ari / Maya —

Great talking earlier. This thread is a concise recap of the agreed POC scope, proposed model choices for the trial, acceptance criteria, ownership, and next steps so we can kick off next week. I pulled our suggested artifacts into the attachments and Drive link.

High-level goal
- Validate that a Redwood-hosted open-model configuration can reliably handle RetailX customer chat flows (EN/ES/FR) with acceptable latency and cost while meeting your quality bar for product recommendations and checkout guidance.

Proposed trial parameters (suggested)
- Duration: 4 weeks (kickoff next Tue 8/10)
- Checkpoints: week 2 midpoint demo + data sync; week 4 final evaluation and decision
- Traffic: 2k sample sessions/day from your anonymized farmed dataset (we'll coordinate sampler)

Model roster (primary + fallback)
- Primary (open, production-tuned): Mistral-8B-Instruct quantized (balanced accuracy + efficiency)
- Fallback (lower latency/cost when needed): OpenAssistant-13B-QLoRA (instruct-tuned)
- Notes: we’ll evaluate both with the same prompt set and use Redwood’s KV/prefix caching for common session flows.

Multilingual needs
- Priority languages: English, Spanish, French (EN/ES/FR). Evaluation will include language-specific test buckets and per-language acceptance thresholds.

Success & evaluation criteria (draft — Laura will formalize rubric)
- Quality: Intent F1 >= 0.88 on core product QA tests; critical intents (checkout/payment) >= 0.92
- Safety: system-level block rate < 1% on sample prompts after filters
- Performance: p95 latency <= 300ms for 512-token horizon on our dedicated endpoint
- Cost: average per-session token cost target <= $0.006 (TBD after exact sample distribution)
- Ops: zero severity incidents during trial; graceful fallback configured for 99.9% of requests under load

Ownership (initial)
- Ben Carter: trial coordinator, SOW/Docusign, weekly checkpoints with RetailX
- Laura Bennett: evaluation rubric, scoring spreadsheet, lead on QA analysis
- Karthik Iyer: infra and quantization config, instance sizing, and canary rollout

Attachments included (stubs)
- POC-success-metrics-worksheet.xlsx (template for scoring)
- model_shortlist.csv (benchmarks & quant configs)
- sample_prompt_set_v1.json (selection of prompts we agreed on during call)

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Ari / Maya: confirm acceptance of the primary/fallback model pairing and the 4-week cadence by EOD Fri 8/6.
2) RetailX: share anonymized sample corpus (S3 link) and the top 12 customer intents by 8/6.
3) Redwood (Karthik): confirm instance sizing + expected latency estimate by Mon 8/9.
4) Ben: circulate SOW for signature once model selection + data access confirmed.

If you prefer a different primary model (e.g., prefer a 13B primary), say so and we’ll swap into the shortlist and re-run lightweight latency/cost checks before kickoff.

Thanks — look forward to getting this scheduled.

Ben

- Model pick: Mistral-8B-Instruct as primary sounds good if it meets the checkout-intent accuracy. We’d like OpenAssistant-13B as an alternate fallback; can you include both in the shortlist?
- Data: I’ll share a scrubbed S3 link with 7k sample sessions and the top 12 intents by Thursday (8/5).
- Compliance: we will need a short note on data retention during the POC (how long you keep logs, who has access) — send a one-pager.

Confirming we’re comfortable with the 4-week window and week-2 check. Please add a short canary plan for the first 48 hours in the SOW.

Ben / team —

I drafted a scoring rubric (high level) and populated the sheet with weightings based on our conversation. I attached a quick snapshot to this reply — full worksheet is in the Drive link. Key points:

Evaluation rubric (proposed weights)
- Overall quality (intent F1 + response correctness): 50%
- Critical intent correctness (checkout/payment/returns): 20%
- Latency & availability: 15%
- Safety / compliance filters: 10%
- Cost efficiency: 5%

Acceptance thresholds (draft)
- Intent F1 (overall): >= 0.88
- Critical intents: >= 0.92
- p95 latency: <= 350ms (we’ll aim for 300ms but hold a 350ms threshold to be practical)
- Safety: false-positive block rate < 1% on allowed prompts

Notes for Karthik
- We should run a 1-hour perf sweep with Mistral-8B quantized on the dedicated endpoint to capture realistic p95 numbers with the expected concurrency. Please confirm instance types and expected token throughput.
- Include KV caching baseline in perf runs (RetailX has many repeated session prefixes).

I’ll own the scoring during the trial and share mid-week dashboards at week 2. Ben, can you add the canary rollout notes Ari requested into the SOW before sending?

Laura Bennett
